posts.title: Early Senate Decisions
posts.description: By Jim Ellis — Wednesday, November 25, 2026 Already, several Senators have announced they will seek re-election in 2028, while others appear prepared to run again but say they will formalize their plans at a later date. The Down-Ballot political blog released a story pinpointing each incumbent Senator and what they have said so far about 2028. No Senate incumbent has yet declared if he or she will retire. Below is a capsule of what The Down-Ballot prognosticators report: Declaring 2028 Candidacy The following Senators have said they will seek re-election in 2028: Richard Blumenthal (D-CT) Brian Schatz (D-HI) Ted Budd (R-NC) Sherrod Brown (D-OH) Ron Wyden (D-OR) Patty Murray (D-WA) Likely to Run The following appear preparing for re-election but have not made a formal statement. posts.title: Presidential Debate Plan Announced
posts.description: By Jim Ellis — Tuesday, November 24, 2026 As was predicted, the beginning of the 2028 open presidential campaign would come soon after the 2026 midterm elections closed, and it appears the Democrats just fulfilled the forecast. Yesterday, Democratic National Committee Chairman Ken Martin announced that the party will hold 12 official presidential primary debates. Five are scheduled for 2027, with the first targeted for an unscheduled date in June. Of the seven primary debates to be held after Jan. 1 and before Super Tuesday (March 7, 2028), six will be held in states with early primary elections. The DNC has released the presidential primary schedule that begins in South Carolina on Jan. 22, 2028. The candidates will then compete in Nevada on Feb. 1, New Hampshire on Feb. 8, New Mexico on the 15th, Michigan, the 22nd, and Virginia on Feb. 29, setting the stage for Super Tuesday.
